Existing legal keys survive create_all adoption/replayed migration. Suspect or duplicate preexisting keys fail closed for explicit repair instead of silent reassignment.

SQLite online Alembic maintenance uses autocommit, disables FK only on its migration connection, starts BEGIN IMMEDIATE, rebuilds the parent, checks foreign_key_check, commits/rolls back, and restores FK ON. Prior migration work is committed before this controlled transaction.
Bot/human/ticket children and ActionLedger.live_session_id must survive the upgrade. Unit fixtures exercised rollback and FK restoration on injected rebuild failures.

Offline SQLite generated SQL was executed locally against legacy fixtures, but an arbitrary external SQL-runner interruption has no Python finally cleanup guarantee; operators must inspect FK-check output.
Downgrade refuses private sessions or any human rows. Empty/public-only guards do not prove reverting an old application image or database backup is generally safe.
